column5: IEEE International Conference on Recent Advances in Science and Engineering Technology, ICRASET 2024
column8: Datasets: No named public anomaly detection benchmark datasets are used in experiments. The paper references medical imaging datasets in the literature review (Brain MRI, head CT, mammography, retinal OCT from cited works) but conducts its own experiments using unspecified medical images processed through the proposed pipeline. Data Types: 2D medical images (X-ray, CT, PET, MRI scans) converted to 3D point cloud and mesh representations; image data. Application Domain: Healthcare / Medical Imaging â€” specifically anomaly detection in biomedical images for tumor detection, fracture identification, rare disease spotting, and clinical diagnosis support.
column10: K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) and Isolation Forest, used sequentially as the base anomaly detectors: the paper states that anomaly detection 'initially employs the K-Nearest-Neighbors (KNN) Algorithm to train the model on normal data' and that 'the isolation forest algorithm enhances accuracy and memory efficiency for more precise results,' with the Isolation Forest computing an anomaly score based on the number of splits needed to isolate a node. Additionally, GAN-based detectors (AnoGAN, f-AnoGAN, ADAE, VQ-GAN, ALAD) and VAE-based detectors are discussed and referenced from the literature as relevant background methods, while the proposed model's generative component uses a GAN (with CNN-based generator and discriminator) combined with a stable diffusion model for the 2D-to-3D conversion step.

column3: Etsebeth, V; Lochner, M.; Walmsley, M.; Grespan, M.
column5: MONTHLY NOTICES OF THE ROYAL ASTRONOMICAL SOCIETY
column8: Datasets: Dark Energy Camera Legacy Survey (DECaLS) DR8 â€” a subset of 3,884,404 resolved galaxy images selected from 871 million sources; an evaluation set of ~5,000 random sources plus 87 gravitational lens candidates from Huang et al. (2020); the Galaxy Zoo dataset is mentioned for prior work comparison. Data Types: Astronomical image data (optical galaxy image cut-outs in g, r, z bands; 150Ã—150 pixel greyscale images after pre-processing); high-dimensional CNN feature vectors (1280-dimensional, reduced to 26 via PCA). Application Domain: Astronomy / Astrophysics â€” specifically anomaly detection in large-scale optical galaxy surveys for scientific discovery (gravitational lenses, galaxy mergers, morphologically unusual sources).
column10: Isolation Forest (iForest), implemented via scikit-learn. iForest is the sole base anomaly detection algorithm used on the main dataset of ~3.9 million sources, selected because it scaled well to the large data volume while Local Outlier Factor (LOF) â€” the only other algorithm tested â€” could not scale to the full dataset. iForest assigns anomaly scores to CNN-extracted feature vectors (after PCA dimensionality reduction) by measuring path length in random decision trees, with shorter paths indicating greater anomalousness. The active learning module (Neighbour Score or Direct Regression) then adjusts these iForest scores based on human labels to re-rank sources.

column1: Bayesian active learning isolation forest (B-ALIF): A weakly supervised strategy for anomaly detection
column3: Sartor, Davide; Barbariol, Tommaso; Susto, Gian Antonio
column5: Engineering Applications of Artificial Intelligence
column8: Datasets: 18 real-world tabular benchmark datasets from the ODDS library (Outlier Detection DataSets, Stony Brook University), including annthyroid, breastw, cardio, cover, ionosphere, letter, mammography, mnist, optdigits, pendigits, pima, satellite, satimage-2, thyroid, vertebral, vowels, wbc, and wine. A synthetic 2D square toroidal dataset is also used for qualitative analysis. Data Types: Tabular feature vectors (multivariate numerical tabular data, derived from multi-class classification problems where one underrepresented class is treated as anomalous). Application Domains: General-purpose anomaly detection across diverse domains including healthcare/medical (annthyroid, breastw, cardio, mammography, thyroid, vertebral, pima), cybersecurity/network (cover, ionosphere, letter), image-based (mnist, optdigits, pendigits, satimage-2, satellite), and others (vowels, wbc, wine); the paper also mentions Decision Support Systems as the primary deployment context.
column10: Isolation Forest (IF) is the sole base anomaly detector, used as both the initialization prior and the underlying tree structure for B-ALIF. The IF constructs the forest of binary trees used by B-ALIF; B-ALIF inherits IF's space partitions entirely and only modifies the abstract node properties (Beta distribution parameters stored at each leaf) through Bayesian updates without restructuring the trees. The paper also compares B-ALIF against ALIF (Active Learning Isolation Forest, the direct predecessor), IF-AAD (Isolation Forest with Active Anomaly Discovery weight optimization), and Î½-SSVM (One-Class SVM variant), but Isolation Forest is the foundational base detector on which B-ALIF is built.

column1: Boundary-Driven Active Learning for Anomaly Detection in Time Series Data Streams
column3: X. Zhou; Y. Wang; H. Xu; M. Liu
column5: ICASSP 2024 - 2024 IEEE International Conference on Acoustics, Speech and Signal Processing (ICASSP)
column8: Datasets: Six public time series datasets streamed in random order to simulate real-time scenarios: sASD (Application Server Dataset), sSMD (Server Machine Dataset), sDSADS (Daily and Sports Activities Dataset), sPSM (Pooled Server Metrics), sMSL (Mars Science Laboratory rover), and sSWaT (Secure Water Treatment testbed). Data Types: Multivariate time series data streams processed as sliding-window samples (D-dimensional observation vectors at each time step, with past windows used as data samples). Application Domains: IT operations / server monitoring (ASD, SMD, PSM), industrial control systems / cyber-physical systems (SWaT â€” water treatment), space / aerospace systems (MSL â€” spacecraft telemetry), and human activity recognition (DSADS).
column10: Deep One-Class Classification (Deep SVDD variant), specifically a neural network Ï• that learns to map data into a hypersphere in a latent feature space, with the hypersphere center c and radius R used to compute anomaly scores as the distance from the mapped representation to the boundary. This is built on the Deep SVDD (DSVDD) and Deep SAD (DSAD) frameworks: DSVDD provides the unsupervised hypersphere initialization and DSAD provides the semi-supervised penalty loss structure for incorporating labeled data. The neural network Ï• constitutes the core base detector, and BALAD extends it with the skip query strategy and boundary-driven feedback strategy on top of this deep one-class classification foundation.

column3: Wang, Xiaoyu; Yang, Xiaobo; Liang, Xueping; Zhang, Xiu; Zhang, Wei; Gong, Xiaorui
column5: COMPUTERS & SECURITY
column8: Datasets: Five alert datasets constructed or adapted for multi-step attack detection: lldos (DARPA 2000 LLDOS1.0, 750 alerts, 51 attack alerts, PCAP processed with Snort 2.9); iscx (UNB ISCX IDS 2012, 12,463 alerts, 107 attack alerts, PCAP processed with Snort 2.9); CPTC-T1 (Collegiate Penetration Testing Competition 2018 Team 1, 85,548 alerts, 1,609 attack alerts, Suricata-generated); CPTC-T5 (142,463 alerts, 2,098 attack alerts); CPTC-T8 (73,046 alerts, 2,067 attack alerts). WIDE MAWI backbone traffic used as background noise for CPTC datasets. Data Types: Network alert/event records in structured format (JSON-based Suricata/Snort alerts), processed as tabular feature vectors with 19 features (basic, context, and history). Application Domain: Cybersecurity / Network Security â€” specifically Security Operations Center (SOC) alert triage and multi-step APT attack detection.
column10: Isolation Forest (IF), implemented via sklearn. IF is the foundational anomaly detection algorithm used in the Alert Ranking module to compute initial anomaly scores for all alerts based on basic and context features; it treats attack alerts as anomalies (rare, distinct points) and all other alerts as normal data. The IF-computed anomaly score is then used as one of the nine state dimensions in the reinforcement learning-based Alert Re-ranking module. One-class SVM is mentioned as an alternative option for the initial ranking but is not the primary base detector used in experiments. Comparator active learning methods AAD and Meta-AAD also use IF as their underlying detector.

column10: DeepSAD (Deep Semi-Supervised Anomaly Detection) by Ruff et al. (2020), implemented with its default hyperparameters. DeepSAD is the core semi-supervised anomaly detector used throughout all experiments in SADAL; it is trained on the unlabeled training set initially and then retrained incrementally as active learning labels are collected from the training set. DeepSAD maps instances to anomaly scores via a deep neural network trained to minimize distances of normal instances to a center in latent space while maximizing distances for labeled anomalies. The paper also references LOF as a motivating example of a heuristic-based unsupervised detector in the introduction, but DeepSAD is the sole base detector used experimentally.
